content.title: Why the World Is Racing to Build Quantum Computers [ID0402]
content.text: Sign in to confirm you’re not a bot This helps protect our community. Learn more What if the computers we use today… aren’t the final form of computing? For decades, every device around us has relied on the same simple rule: everything is either a **0 or a 1**. But deep in the strange world of quantum physics, nature doesn’t always follow those rules. Scientists are now building machines that don’t just process one possibility at a time. Instead, they explore **many possibilities at once**. These machines are called **quantum computers**, and they could one day solve problems that today’s most powerful supercomputers would struggle with for thousands of years. But how can a computer be both **0 and 1 at the same time**? And why are some of the world’s biggest tech companies racing to build one?
